Rotations

Each team member's repeating schedule. Build a pattern once — it stays attached to that person.

Set a pattern up once on one person, then copy it to everyone who works the same pattern.

Assign vacation or leave. Add as many date ranges as you need — the rotation automatically resumes after each one. Delete a vacation to put the person back on their regular rotation.

Add vacation

Scheduled skips

Groups are ordered lists of team members. Point a group rotation at a group and its members take turns working that shift — in this order, all the time. Admins and schedulers decide who is in each group.

New group

Name the group, then tick its people — pick a department to look through, switch departments to add people from anywhere, or upload a file of names/emails. The order people are picked in is the order they take turns.

New rotation

Copy a rotation to people

Pre-filled with the original's start date so everyone's cycles stay in step. Each copy is independent afterwards. Vacations, one-off changes and draft/publish tweaks on the original are not copied.

Inverse gives the other person the days this pattern does NOT work, inside the same cycle. Example: 7 days on / 7 days off — the other person gets the 7 off days as their working week. If the pattern works Mon–Fri every week, the inverse is Sat–Sun every week. For the same days on alternate weeks, use Pairing instead.

Pair people on a pattern

Pairing connects people to one pattern and deals its working turns between them, in order. Example: the pattern works 1 week, off 1 week — the first person takes week 1, the second takes week 3, the first takes week 5. If the pattern works every week, they alternate every week and the slot is never empty. What the pair's calendar looks like depends on the pattern you set.

Pre-filled with the original's start date so the pair runs in step with the pattern. The pair is its own rotation afterwards — find it with the group rotations, and the people under Groups.

Change rotation from a date

The current rotation stops the day before this date — everything before stays exactly as it was. Shifts already saved as real shifts are never touched; this changes the pattern only.

Swap rotations from a date

Tick 2 or more people in the order of the swap. From the chosen date, each person takes the next person's pattern, starting fresh on that date — the last person takes the first person's. Everything before that date stays exactly as it was, and shifts already saved as real shifts are never touched.

New group rotation

Each turn goes to the next group. Inside a group, the next person in its order takes that group's turn — so a group can work a week, rest while the next group works, then come back with its next person. If the person whose turn is starting is on vacation, the next person in line takes the whole turn, and the person on vacation takes the next turn instead.

Email Q-Scheduler notifications

For each department, choose who gets the Email Q-Scheduler approve/reject emails. The primary recipient is in To:, CCs are in Cc:. The owner is always CC'd. The person who sent the request always gets a confirmation.

Email inbox

Connect this company's own Gmail mailbox so Email Q-Scheduler reads your schedule emails — not a shared inbox. The app checks it every 5 minutes and builds plans for your approval; it never changes the schedule on its own.

To connect:

  1. In that Gmail account, turn on 2-Step Verification.
  2. Go to Google Account → Security → App passwords and generate one for "Mail".
  3. Paste the 16 characters here (spaces are fine).

Use an app password, never the account's normal password. The password is stored encrypted and is never shown back.

Poll this inbox for schedule emails

Meeting services

Connect Zoom, Microsoft Teams or Google Meet once and the event form grows a one-tap button for that service: it creates the meeting for the session's date and time and fills in the link. If the session's time changes, its meeting updates too. Only the owner connects or disconnects a service; after that, the buttons work for everyone who can edit the session.

What the admin view looks like

        

          

            
            
Admin: Schedule tab with tabs, filters, and shift boxes you can tap to edit

          

          

            
            
Admin: Ask Q-Scheduler — plain-language questions, instant answers

          

        

      


      

        
Schedule views

        

          
Week view — Day/Week/Month/Range tabs, Department and Shift filters

          
Settings → Shifts — define your own shift types, colors, and times

          
Settings → Staffing — daily targets per shift type, highlights short-staffed days

        

        
The Schedule tab has three views: Day, Week, and Range.

        
    
          
  • Day view — see everyone scheduled for one date. Tap a shift box to reassign, swap, or remove someone. The round down-arrow button at the right of a shift box opens its actions (highlight, comment, publish, replace, delete).
    • 
          
  • Week view — seven days at a glance with full shift names.
    • 
          
  • Range view — pick any date range.
    • 
        

        
Filter by Department or Shift using the two dropdowns under the heading. Green dates are published, gray are draft, plain are empty.

        
Publishing: assign shifts as drafts, then publish each shift when it's final. Staff only see published shifts on shared links — the date itself doesn't need to be published.

      


      

        
Ask Q-Scheduler

        

          
Ask Q-Scheduler — plain-language questions, instant answers

        

        
Ask plain-language questions about the schedule, like "Who is on tonight?", "Where are we short next week?", or "How many shifts did Priya work in September?" Answers cover the whole schedule; draft shifts are labeled (draft).

        
Staffing targets: set how many people you need per shift type per day (e.g. 4 Day Hospitalists + 1 Night Hospitalist + 1 Night NP). Ask "where are we short?" to find gaps.

        
Change plans (email-to-schedule)

        
Forward a schedule email to your connected inbox address and the system reads it, builds a proposed change plan, and emails you for approval — you never have to check email yourself.

        
    
          
  • Change requests ("assign Maya to Day Hospitalist on Oct 12") → a plan appears under Change plans and you get an email with Approve & Apply / Reject buttons that work right from the email.
    • 
          
  • Schedule questions ("send me the schedule for Oct 11–14") → the sender gets an automatic reply with the schedule. Draft shifts are labeled (draft).
    • 
          
  • Plans show who requested the change (name, email, and CC).
    • 
        

      


      

        
Team members & Invite new team members

        

          
Team members — profiles, invites, and status

          
Invite new team members — share the application link, review candidates

        

        
Team members — add people manually or approve them from the candidate queue. Each member sets their own password via an email invite.

        
Invite new team members — people apply through your application link. New applications email you a Review Application link where you can edit their details and Approve or Reject without logging in. Approving creates their team member account and sends them an invite.

        
Set special instructions per member and an optional end date (stops future shifts, keeps history).

      


      

        
Rotations

        

          
Rotations — repeating patterns per team member

        

        
Build repeating patterns (1–84 days) under Settings → Rotations. Assign team members to cycle days and the schedule fills in automatically. Manual shifts always take precedence over rotation-generated ones.

        
You can pause a rotation for vacations and exclude individual rotation instances (e.g. someone swapped out for one day).

      


      

        
Sharable Links

        

          
Sharable Links — schedule, availability, and open-slot links

        

        
Links your team opens with their own sign-in:

        
    
          
  • Schedule link — view-only schedule; the viewer signs in with their account, and only people at your company can open it. Filter by department or shift type.
    • 
          
  • Open shifts broadcast — generate a message listing open shifts for a date range, ready to copy-paste to a group chat.
    • 
          
  • Availability link — staff mark themselves available/unavailable for dates you choose; you see responses per person.
    • 
        

      


      

        
Payroll

        
Pick a date range to see hours by date plus per-person totals. Filter by person, download a PDF, or email the report. Automatic weekly/monthly payroll emails can be scheduled from the payroll tab.

      


      

        
Run report (audit log)

        
The Run report button (top of every tab, bottom of the Schedule page, and on each date popup) shows who changed the schedule — what changed, when, who did it, and whether it was manual or from a rotation. Tracking started October 9, 2026.

      


      


      


      

        
What the employee view looks like

        

          

            
            
Employee: shared schedule link — clean view-only schedule, sign in with your account

          

          

            
            
Employee: availability link — sign in, then tap dates for can-work / can't-work

          

        

      


      

        
Viewing your schedule

        
Your scheduler shares a schedule link with you — no login needed. Open it on your phone or computer to see your upcoming shifts. Only published shifts are shown, so what you see is final.

        
On phones, swipe sideways to move between days, or tap a date in the mini calendar at the top to jump straight to it.

      


      

        
Marking your availability

        
When your scheduler sends an availability link, open it and mark yourself available or unavailable for each date. Your scheduler sees everyone's responses and builds the schedule from them.

        
Submit early — late responses may miss the scheduling window.

      


      

        
Setting up your account

        
If your scheduler adds you as a team member, you'll get an invite email. Click the link to set your own password. Your email is your username.

      


      

        
Requesting schedule changes

        
Need a swap or a day off? Email your scheduler — the system reads schedule emails automatically. For swaps, include who you'd like to swap with and the date. You'll be notified once it's approved.

        
You can also email a question like "Am I scheduled next weekend?" and get an automatic reply with your shifts.

      


      

        
Applying for a job

        
Applied through a company's application link? You'll get an email invite if you're approved. Check your spam folder if you don't see it within a few days.

My settings

        
Your personal account settings. These apply only to you.


        

          
👤 Profile

          

            
            
            
            
Q-Scheduler accepts your requests from your account email above. If you also email it from another address, add that address here so those emails are accepted too.

            
            
            
          

          

            
            
          

          
Name, department and job role are managed by your scheduler — ask them if those need a change.

        


        

          
🔔 Notifications

          
Everything always appears under the 🔔 bell in the app. These settings control the email copies. Daily digest sends one email each morning (~7 AM) with everything from the last day — the bell still records everything right away.

          

          
⏰ Reminders (just for you)

          
Pick up to 2 times for each row — reminders are personal, nobody sets them for you. They always email right away, never in the digest.

          

          
📱 Push notifications (this device)

          
Also get the instant ones as a push on this device — the same notifications that email right away. The daily digest stays email-only.

📅 Calendar feed

          
See your shifts and sessions on your own Google, Outlook or Apple calendar. Subscribe to your private feed link in your calendar app — it keeps itself up to date. Anyone who has the link can see your shifts, so keep it to yourself.

          

            
            
            
          

          
          

            
Google Calendar: Settings → Add calendar → From URL → paste the link.

            
Outlook: Add calendar → Subscribe from web → paste the link.

            
Apple Calendar: File → New Calendar Subscription → paste the link.

Ask Q-Scheduler

        

          

            
            
Ask Q-Scheduler — plain-language questions, instant answers

          

          

            
            
Email Q-Scheduler — write your request, it opens your email app

          

          

            
            
The Email Q-Scheduler button floats at the bottom-right of every screen

          

        

        
Ask plain-language questions about the schedule, like "Who's working on October 14?" or "Am I scheduled next weekend?"

        
The Email Q-Scheduler button (also floating at the bottom-right of every screen) opens a short form — pick what you need (a day off, a swap, a session change, a question) from your own calendar, check the preview, and send. The form is read exactly, first time, and your request goes straight to your scheduler for approval. Prefer your own words? You can still email the scheduler in plain words instead, and from the "free-text email" option in the form you can also attach a file — a PDF, an Excel sheet, a CSV or a Word document (for example a whole schedule) — and the AI reads the attachment as part of your request.
